The longstanding CBO/JCT/Treasury OTA convention that a policy change does not alter total nominal income, so duty paid is income not paid to labour and capital and the income and payroll tax bases shrink. Cited secondhand: jct.gov and cbo.gov both return HTTP 403 to this environment, so the primary - JCT, 'The Income and Payroll Tax Offset to Changes in Excise Tax Revenues' (JCX-59-11) - was not read directly. Lane R8 replaced the round 0.25 with JCT's own PUBLISHED YEAR PATH, which ships inside CBO's Conventional Tariff Analysis Model at inputs/offset/2025OffsetPostHR1.csv (commit 59ea68fd) and is applied there one year at a time at code/model/add_offset.py:18. The path runs 0.244 (2025) to 0.241 (2035); this value is its mean over the library default window FY2025-2034, and the scoring chain reads the path over each policy's own window rather than this key. column6: The repository's own knowledge snapshot, fiscal_model/assistant/knowledge/tariff_scoring_methodology.md, puts a fully-netted tariff score at 40-50% of gross customs revenue. Lane H8 found that comparing the module's net_to_gross_ratio against this band is a DENOMINATOR MISMATCH: the snapshot's chain is gross ~$3.0T -> $2.2T after the demand response -> $1.7T after GDP feedback -> $1.2-1.5T with retaliation, so its denominator is gross BEFORE the demand response while the module's is after it. On the snapshot's own denominator the universal preset reads 0.589 conventionally and 0.485 dynamic-with-retaliation - inside the band, not above it. The 40-50% is the snapshot's own synthesis, not a sentence quoted from any single agency document
